messages:
incident_bot: ALERT — GPU autoscale alert: inference-pool queue > 95% for 7m, HPA reporting 0 desired replicas due to metrics unavailable. Severity: P1 :rotating_light:

maria: ack — paging infra oncall now. seeing spike in customer 42 latency and 429s. routing & throttling kicking in.

ahmed: on it, checking prometheus and metrics-adapter. grabbing logs.

kevin: ping @maria if you need manual scale, I can run `kubectl scale` and warm GPUs.

maria: yes please. if HPA is stuck we need manual scale to keep tail latency down. also notify support to surface impacted customers.

ahmed: prometheus scrape lag high for nodes, several `up` targets show 503. adapter logs: ```
E0912 10:15:23.123456       1 adapter.go:142] error querying metrics: context deadline exceeded
E0912 10:15:23.123457       1 adapter.go:167] failed to fetch custom metrics for HorizontalPodAutoscaler: metrics API error: no metrics returned
```

ahmed: metric name the HPA uses is `redwood_inference_gpu_queue_length`. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/abcd/inference-autoscale?from=now-30m (posted)

ops_robin: support notified customers in impacted orgs, posting interim guidance: reduce concurrency or switch to fallback endpoint.

julie: logs from metrics-adapter pod show repeated 504s from prometheus-query service. suspect prometheus scale or remote-write backlog.

maria: ok, mitigation plan: (1) manual scale inference-pool to +3 replicas (2) restart metrics-adapter (3) if prometheus is overloaded, flip HPA to use approximate `queue_length_estimate` from sidecar (fallback metric) and add admission note.

kevin: running manual scale now: `kubectl scale deploy/inference-pool --replicas=12 -n inference` — I see new pods scheduling.

sre_bot: deploybot: started rollout for scaled replicas at 10:18 UTC.

ahmed: restarting metrics-adapter pod (pod/metrics-adapter-7b9d8). restarting...

ahmed: metrics-adapter is back up but logs still show some slow queries. running `curl -s http://localhost:443/metrics` on adapter shows metrics exposed.

maria: can we confirm HPA read metrics after restart?

ahmed: checking HPA status: ```
kubectl get hpa inference-pool-hpa -n inference -o yaml
# status:
#   currentMetrics: []
#   conditions:
#   - type: AbleToScale
#     status: "False"
#     message: "unable to get metrics for resource \"redwood_inference_gpu_queue_length\""
```

ahmed: still not reading the custom metric — adapter returns values when queried locally but the metrics API path is timing out intermittently. suspect prometheus query front-door overloaded.

ryan: thought: we have an older adapter config that hits Prometheus /api/v1/query with large cardinality; we can switch to a pre-aggregated metric in redis for a short window. ops_robin can we flip a feature flag to let HPA use `queue_len_approx` from redis?

ops_robin: I can patch the HPA to the fallback metric but need approval — this changes autoscale semantics.

maria: do it. we need autoscale working. patch HPA to use `queue_len_approx` with target 80. also set cooldown to 60s.

kevin: patch applied: `kubectl patch hpa inference-pool-hpa --patch 'spec:{metrics:[{type:External,external:{metric:{name:"queue_len_approx"},target:{type:AverageValue,averageValue:"80"}}}]}'`

sre_bot: hpa-bot: HPA patched successfully.

julie: after patch, HPA shows desired 14 replicas and is scaling. queue length trending down on grafana. :white_check_mark:

ahmed: good. manual scale will be reversed once HPA stable. still need to investigate why prometheus query latency spiked — could be retention compaction or remote_write backlog.

maria: interim customer impact summary: ~8 customers saw tail latency >5s, 3 reported 429s; no data loss. support ticket IDs: #INC-1023, #INC-1024.

ops_robin: mitigation notes posted to runbook channel and support playbook updated with fallback HPA metric steps.

kevin: on-call handoff: I'm taking next 30m to monitor. @maria can you do final handoff and include action items?

maria: handing off to kevin at 10:45 UTC — key actions: (1) postmortem to investigate prometheus cardinality and query load (2) add circuit-breaker to adapter queries (3) add synthetic metrics to ensure HPA fallback path is exercised in canary, (4) consider autoscale based on prefix-KV cache hit rate to reduce queue pressure.

ahmed: I'll open a follow-up ticket to repro the adapter timeouts: `INF-789` with logs attached.

julie: ops note — we should add alert for `metrics_adapter_query_latency > 2s` and escalate before HPA fails.

kevin: monitoring: will keep dashboard pinned and watch that `queue_len_approx` and `gpu_util` correlate. Also will scale down manual replicas slowly once HPA holds.

maria: thanks everyone. post-incident: calendar invite for incident review tomorrow 11:00 UTC. assigning owners: prometheus scale (ahmed), adapter hardening (julie), HPA runbook updates (maria).

incident_bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigated: traffic routed and autoscale fallback enabled. status: monitoring.

kevin: closing thread for now, will reopen if regressions. :thumbsup:
